newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commissioners' Gibraltar visit angers Spain.
newsitem.headline: Commissioners' Gibraltar visit angers Spain.

text.p: Spain's sensitivity over Gibraltar spilled over onto the European Commission on Tuesday when Madrid complained angrily about a visit to the disputed British colony by Swedish Commissioner Anita Gradin.
Gradin, who is responsible for crime and judicial affairs, viisted Gibraltar on November 4 to study how it fights illegal drug trafficking from North Africa.

Spain's ambassador to the European Union, Javier Elorza, said he had protested orally to the Commission about the visit, in particular what he said was an unscheduled inspection by Gradin of a Spanish customs and border post.
Although this had been done with the approval of the local customs chief, Elorza said EU rules required three months notice for such a visit.
A spokewoman for Gradin said the commissioner had gone to Gibraltar as part of her responsibilities to work against drug smuggling on the EU's borders. She had earlier visited Morocco.
"It was a fact-finding mission," the spokeswoman said, adding that it had included a trip on the high-speed boats used in the region in the fight against the drugs trade.
Spain claims sovereignty over the colony at its southern tip which has been ruled by Britain for nearly 300 years.
Elorza said Madrid was angry that Gradin has chosen to study drug fighting from the other side of the border. Spain blames Gibraltar for much of the smuggling that pervades the region.
"For Spain, it is peculiar that she went to Gibraltar rather than to us," he said.
